issues.problem: party_name is an IP filing applicant/owner name, and the config itself says it is not labelled as registered. The ontology defines legal_name as the registered name, so this maps a claim the source does not make. The example 'tb12f486a1f25d910ea322ef708a01486' is a hash-like string, not a name at all, and is emitted as legal_name.

The envelope shown for each observation carries only observed_at, valid_from and valid_to. The ontology requires source_id, source_record_id, observed_at, ingested_at, licence and extractor_version on every record, with no exceptions. source_id, source_record_id, ingested_at, licence and extractor_version are missing from the examples and the config does not define them.

The ABN transform does not check lord_party_id_type=abn, even though the config says the flag is what distinguishes ABNs from internal ids. The regex only restricts the value to 11 digits before the '.0', so an internal id that happens to be 11 digits would pass to the checksum and rely on the checksum alone to reject it. The type flag is listed as unmapped, so it is never used.

entity_type 'unknown' is emitted with from: null on every row. That is a default, not a source claim, yet it is written as an observation with a null source column, which could be mistaken for a sourced value.

observed_at is taken from resource_last_modified (2023-08-29) while the counts describe financial years 2003 to 2005. The ontology says observed_at is when the source stated the claim, and the metadata date is when the file was last changed, which is a different thing.

No confidence fields (source_reliability, field_confidence, link_confidence) are set on the examples. The ABN-to-entity claim and the free-text name claim carry very different reliability, and the name claim is not checked at all.

Some values are abbreviated or informal, such as 'quality innovations p/l' and 'five hats wine co'. Even where the name is a real business name, it is not the registered form (for example 'Pty Ltd' in place of 'p/l').

critique_issues.problem: party_name is an IP filing applicant/owner name, and the config itself says it is not labelled as registered. The ontology defines legal_name as the registered name, so this maps a claim the source does not make. The example 'tb12f486a1f25d910ea322ef708a01486' is a hash-like string, not a name at all, and is emitted as legal_name.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Do not emit entity.legal_name from party_name. Emit it as an applicant/owner name observation under a non-legal field, or map to trading_name with a low field_confidence, and drop or quarantine hash-like values.

critique_issues.problem: The envelope shown for each observation carries only observed_at, valid_from and valid_to. The ontology requires source_id, source_record_id, observed_at, ingested_at, licence and extractor_version on every record, with no exceptions. source_id, source_record_id, ingested_at, licence and extractor_version are missing from the examples and the config does not define them.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Add source_id, a deterministic source_record_id built from lord_party_id, financial_year and the row position, ingested_at, licence (from CKAN metadata, or 'unknown' and flagged) and extractor_version to every emitted observation.

critique_issues.problem: The ABN transform does not check lord_party_id_type=abn, even though the config says the flag is what distinguishes ABNs from internal ids. The regex only restricts the value to 11 digits before the '.0', so an internal id that happens to be 11 digits would pass to the checksum and rely on the checksum alone to reject it. The type flag is listed as unmapped, so it is never used.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Gate the entity.abn transform on lord_party_id_type == 'abn' before applying the regex and checksum, and use the type flag explicitly rather than unmapping it.

critique_issues.problem: entity_type 'unknown' is emitted with from: null on every row. That is a default, not a source claim, yet it is written as an observation with a null source column, which could be mistaken for a sourced value.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Either omit the observation when there is no source value, or mark it explicitly as a defaulted value (for example derivation_level L1 with a note that it is a default), so it is not read as a statement from the source.

critique_issues.problem: observed_at is taken from resource_last_modified (2023-08-29) while the counts describe financial years 2003 to 2005. The ontology says observed_at is when the source stated the claim, and the metadata date is when the file was last changed, which is a different thing.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Keep the metadata timestamp, but document in the config that it is the publication date, and consider recording financial_year as a separate reporting-period field so the observation time is not read as the time the party was observed.

critique_issues.problem: No confidence fields (source_reliability, field_confidence, link_confidence) are set on the examples. The ABN-to-entity claim and the free-text name claim carry very different reliability, and the name claim is not checked at all.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Set source_reliability per publisher, field_confidence per field (lower for party_name, higher for checksum-validated ABNs), and leave link_confidence unset unless the record is linked to an entity.

critique_issues.problem: Some values are abbreviated or informal, such as 'quality innovations p/l' and 'five hats wine co'. Even where the name is a real business name, it is not the registered form (for example 'Pty Ltd' in place of 'p/l').
critique_issues.suggested_fix: If any legal-name-like field is kept, normalise known suffixes (p/l to Pty Ltd, pty. limited to Pty Ltd) and record the raw value, with the normalisation at derivation_level L1.

abstentions.reason: Source names are IP filing applicant/owner names, not stated as registered names; some are hash-like strings.
Source does not say the name is a trading name.
